title: Ramayana Trailer to Debut at San Diego Comic-Con on July 24 in Historic First for Indian Cinema
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's epic starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash will premiere its trailer at SDCC's Ballroom 20, marking the most ambitious international launch for a Bollywood film.
body:
Comic-Con Premiere Marks Strategic Shift

The makers of Ramayana: Part 1 have confirmed that the film's official trailer will debut at San Diego Comic-Con 2026 on July 23 (July 24 IST) in the prestigious Ballroom 20. Producer Namit Malhotra, director Nitesh Tiwari, and the principal cast will present the panel, making it one of the highest-profile international debuts for an Indian film in history.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=vDXjx5Hbe5o

The decision to launch at SDCC rather than a domestic venue represents a deliberate pivot by Prime Focus Studios. The producers shifted from a planned domestic-only rollout to an international platform, positioning Ramayana not as a regional film but as a global civilizational epic aimed at audiences worldwide.

The move follows the film's earlier teaser, which showed Ranbir Kapoor in his first look as Lord Rama and racked up 18 million YouTube views within 24 hours of release in April.

A Cast Built for Scale

Ramayana features one of the most ambitious ensembles in Indian cinema. Ranbir Kapoor, who reportedly spent months on physical and dialect training, plays Lord Rama. Sai Pallavi takes on the role of Sita, Kannada superstar Yash plays Ravana, Sunny Deol appears as Hanuman, and Ravi Dubey plays Lakshman. Rakul Preet Singh and Kunal Kapoor round out the supporting cast.

https://x.com/indiaforums/status/2079841937805246474

The film's music carries its own star power. Oscar-winning composer Hans Zimmer is collaborating with A.R. Rahman on the score and background music — a pairing that has drawn significant international attention and underscored the project's crossover ambitions.

Box Office Expectations

Trade experts are projecting a massive opening. The film is set for a Diwali 2026 theatrical release, with reports indicating the makers may prepone to October 30 — a week before the festival — to build word-of-mouth momentum during the extended holiday period.

Industry analysts expect the film to challenge the ₹100 crore net mark on opening day, with some suggesting it could push toward ₹150 crore if the trailer generates strong response.

Distribution negotiations for a deal reportedly worth around ₹450 crore are underway, highlighting the enormous financial stakes. The film topped IMDb's Most Anticipated Indian Movies of 2026 list and is being backed by Prime Focus Studios and Monster Mind Creations. Backed by cutting-edge visual effects, it is positioned as one of the most expensive Indian films ever produced.

What's Next

All eyes turn to Ballroom 20 at SDCC on July 23. The trailer will offer the first detailed look at the film's storytelling, action sequences, and visual ambition. A second instalment is already planned for Diwali 2027. Meanwhile, the makers are running a Colours of Ramayana art contest, offering Indian school students a chance to win exclusive merchandise and early trailer screenings back home.
nri_angle: The SDCC premiere signals a strategic shift in how Indian cinema reaches global audiences, particularly diaspora viewers.
author: Diaspora Desk
